QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_46

question.text: A farmer is worried that the price of wheat may fall by the time of harvest. Which derivative instrument can the farmer use to protect against this price risk?

answer.text: Sell wheat futures contracts to lock in a predetermined price for the harvest
Buy equity shares of a wheat processing company
Open a bank fixed deposit to earn fixed interest
Purchase government bonds with a 10-year maturity

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures are agreements to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price and date. Derivatives transfer risk from those who wish to avoid it to those willing to bear it, and commodity derivatives let participants hedge against commodity-price fluctuations. By selling wheat futures, the farmer locks in a predetermined price for the harvest. The Trap: Buying equity (option B) exposes the farmer to different risks, not wheat-price risk. FDs (option C) and government bonds (option D) are investment instruments, not hedges against commodity-price movement. Note: The hedge works because the futures position offsets adverse movements in the spot price of wheat over the harvest horizon.
